newsitem.title: USA: Murder charge for British nanny in baby's death.
newsitem.headline: Murder charge for British nanny in baby's death.

text.p: An 18-year-old British nanny will be charged with murder after a nine-month-old boy left in her care died at a Boston hospital from head injuries, prosecutors said on Tuesday.

Louise Woodward, 18, of Chester, England, was already being held on $100,000 bail on a charge of assault. She was arrested a day after the infant, Matthew Eappen, was taken to Children's Hospital in Boston. He died late on Sunday.
"She will not be formally charged with murder until she is arraigned before a judge in District Court Thursday afternoon," said Jill Reilly, a spokeswoman for the Middlesex County District Attorney.
An autopsy showed the death of the child was due to "a blunt force trauma to the head," Assistant District Attorney Lynn Rooney told reporters at a news conference at Newton's Police Headquarters.
The severity of the murder charge will be left up to a grand jury, prosecutors said. "We only present evidence to the grand jury and let them decide the degree," Rooney said.

Conviction on a charge of first-degree murder carries a mandatory life prison sentence without parole, while conviction on a charge of second-degree murder can be punished by up to 30 years in prison with possible parole. There is no mandated minimum prison time for a charge of manslaughter in Massachusetts.
Woodward, who came to the United States in June and had worked for Drs. Sunil and Deborah Eappen since November, remains in a Framingham, Massachusetts, prison.

The Eappens visited the Newton Police Headquarters earlier on Tuesday to confer with prosecutors and police and then were escorted to their white Cape Cod-style home in the Boston suburb of Newton without speaking to reporters.
"It's a very difficult time for them. They do not want to have anything further to do with the media," Rooney said.
